# s439 — ai hooks: a project-local Claude Code hooks snippet

`slicer ai hooks` prints a Claude Code hooks snippet for this project: a SessionStart hook that feeds `slicer ai getting-started` into a new session's context when `.slicer/` exists, and a PreToolUse hook that denies Read, Grep, Edit and Write on slicer's tracking files with a reason that names the CLI read to use instead. `--install` merges it into the project's `.claude/settings.json`, never `~/.claude`, refusing a conflicting slicer entry unless `--force`.

## Why

Owner request 2026-11-02, decision 3: add `slicer ai hooks [--install] [--force]`, which prints or installs a project-local Claude Code hooks snippet, for example SessionStart pointing at `slicer ai getting-started` when `.slicer` exists, and a PreToolUse guard denying Read/Grep/Edit/Write on `.slicer/*.json`, `log.jsonl` and `render/`. Project-local `.claude/settings.json` only, never `~/.claude`; merge-safe (refuse on conflict, `--force` semantics like `ai skill --install`). Codex and Grok parity is out of scope.

The tracking rule (never open `.slicer/` state) is today enforced only by prose in the skill, AGENTS.md and `ai instructions`; agents still open the files (this repo's memory has a standing rule about it). A harness-level deny turns the rule into a refusal with a pointer to the right command.

Claude Code hooks format, verified 2026-11-02 from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions:

- Settings files: `~/.claude/settings.json` (all projects), `.claude/settings.json` (one project, committable), `.claude/settings.local.json` (one project, not shared). Hook entries from different levels merge rather than replace.
- Shape: `{"hooks": {"EVENT": [{"matcher": "...", "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "...", "timeout": N}]}]}}`. Optional handler fields include `args` (exec form, no shell), `shell` (`bash` default), `if` (one permission rule such as `Edit(*.ts)`, tool events only), `async`, `statusMessage`, `once`.
- `command` without `args` is shell form: run by `sh -c` on macOS and Linux (Git Bash, else PowerShell, on Windows); `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is set to the project root where the session started. With `args`, `command` is spawned directly with no shell.
- Matcher: only letters, digits, `_`, `-`, spaces, `,` and `|` is an exact name or list (`Read|Grep|Edit|Write`); any other character makes it an unanchored JavaScript regex.
- SessionStart: matcher values `startup`, `resume`, `clear`, `compact`, `fork`; stdin carries `source`. Plain stdout is added to Claude's context; JSON `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` does the same. No blocking. Only `command` and `mcp_tool` handlers.
- PreToolUse stdin: `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `permission_mode`, `hook_event_name`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_use_id`. `tool_input.file_path` (always absolute) for Read, Write and Edit; Grep has `pattern`, optional `path`, optional `glob`; Glob has `pattern` and optional `path`.
- PreToolUse deny: print `{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "deny", "permissionDecisionReason": "..."}}` and exit 0, or exit 2 with the reason on stderr; both block the call and show Claude the reason. Decisions are `allow`, `deny`, `ask`, `defer`; across hooks `deny` wins. A non-zero exit other than 2 is a non-blocking error.
- Alternative native mechanism: `permissions.deny` rules such as `Read(/.slicer/**/*.json)` (a leading `/` is relative to the settings file's project); Edit rules cover every built-in edit tool, Read rules apply to Grep and Glob only "best-effort".

## Files

- `src/slicer/ai.py` (pure, no state import):
  - `HOOK_SESSION_START = '[ -d "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.slicer" ] && slicer ai getting-started || true'` and `HOOK_GUARD = "slicer ai guard"` (shell form, `slicer` on PATH).
  - `hooks_settings() -> dict` returning, in this key order:

    ```json
    {
      "hooks": {
        "SessionStart": [
          {"matcher": "startup|clear|compact",
           "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": HOOK_SESSION_START, "timeout": 30}]}
        ],
        "PreToolUse": [
          {"matcher": "Read|Grep|Edit|Write",
           "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": HOOK_GUARD, "timeout": 10}]}
        ]
      }
    }
    ```
  - `GUARD_REASON` (one sentence naming `slicer show ID --json --lean`, `slicer list --json --lean`, `slicer log --json --lean` and `slicer ai instructions`) and `guard_decision(payload: Mapping, root: Path) -> str | None`: `None` to allow, else the reason. Denied paths, resolved against `root` (from `payload["cwd"]`, falling back to `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, discovered upward to the directory holding `.slicer/config.json`): any `*.json` anywhere under `.slicer/` (index, config, relay-roles and every slice under `slices/`), `.slicer/log.jsonl`, and anything under `.slicer/render/`. For Read, Edit and Write the path is `tool_input.file_path`; for Grep it is `tool_input.path`, denied when it is `.slicer` itself, `.slicer/slices`, `.slicer/render` or a denied file, or when `tool_input.glob` with `path` under `.slicer` could match a denied file. `.slicer/templates/` and `.slicer/prompts/` stay readable. A path outside `root` is allowed.
- `src/slicer/cli.py`:
  - `cmd_ai_hooks(args)` and an `aisub` parser `hooks` with `--install` and `--force` (help text mirroring `ai skill`). Without `--install` it prints `jsonio.dumps(ai.hooks_settings())` and writes nothing; `--json` returns `{"settings": SNIPPET}`, and with `--install` `{"settings": SNIPPET, "written": [PATHS]}` (empty when nothing changed). `--force` without `--install` is `usage`. `--install` needs a project (`store.discover`; none is `state`) and targets `PROJECT/.claude/settings.json` only.
  - Merge rules for `--install`: a missing file is created (parents too) holding the snippet. An existing file must parse as a JSON object, else `state` naming the file, nothing written. `hooks` and each event list are created if absent; every other key and every other group keep their content and order. A group whose handlers are exactly the snippet's for that event is already installed. A group with a handler whose `command` contains `slicer ai getting-started` or `slicer ai guard` but differs from the snippet is a conflict: exit 2 `state`, the message names the file and the events, nothing written, unless `--force`, which replaces those groups in place with the snippet's. Otherwise the snippet's group is appended to the event list. The result is written with `jsonio.write` (indent 2, trailing newline) only when it differs from the parsed file; text output lists the path written or says it is already installed. No lock (it writes no `.slicer/` state), like `ai skill --install`.
  - `cmd_ai_guard(args)` and an `aisub` parser `guard` (no `--json`: its stdout is the hook protocol). It reads one JSON object from stdin; on a deny it prints the `hookSpecificOutput` deny object (keys `hookEventName`, `permissionDecision`, `permissionDecisionReason`) and exits 0; on an allow it prints nothing and exits 0. Malformed stdin, a non-object, or a tool it does not judge prints nothing and exits 0 (fail open, owner question).
- `tests/test_ai_hooks.py` (new).
- Docs: `docs/commands.md` rows `ai hooks [--install] [--force]` and `ai guard`; `docs/agents.md` JSON row for `ai hooks`, a paragraph after the `ai skill` paragraph with the snippet and the merge rules, and the "Every subcommand except ..." sentence gains `ai guard` (also in `README.md`, `docs/commands.md` and `docs/import.md`, which `test_AgentsDoc_JsonExceptions_MatchParser` checks); `docs/working-with-agents.md`: one line suggesting `slicer ai hooks --install`; `CHANGELOG.md` `## [Unreleased]` `### Added`.
